messages.subject: continue, break, and goto?
parts:
[moving discussion to stan-dev]

On 6/24/13 6:08 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:

> I didn't see a continue in the modeling language specification -- is there one hidden but not documented?

Nope. No continue, break, or goto yet.

They'd be easy to add, of course. Feel free to add
them to the to-do list. I can knock off this kind of
stuff pretty quickly. Though I'm not sure it's a great
idea.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] continue, break, and goto?
parts:
continue and break would be useful, but I'm hesitant to support adding goto because it's just bad practice, particularly in a language as high level as Stan.  Goto would also require that we add annotations to the langue, to mark locations to which to go.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] continue, break, and goto?
parts:
On 6/24/13 8:55 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> continue and break would be useful, but I'm hesitant to support adding goto because it's just bad practice, particularly
> in a language as high level as Stan. Goto would also require that we add annotations to the langue, to mark locations
> to which to go.

That's my feeling, too. Unlikely anyone's going to need
to implement a crazy enough algorithm that they need goto (though
it can be useful).

I'll drop these onto the to do list. Shouldn't be hard to add
at all as they'll translate directly into C++. I've seen a lot
of inexperienced programmers get confused about the scope of
break and continue relative to conditionals, but then it's unlikely
most of our users are going to use them anyway.

- Bob
